_comment: Row-level access for the CONSOLE (a signed-in person in a browser). Read-only, and
scoped to rows the caller owns.
Read-only is the design, not a limitation: every write in DutyBoard is a state-machine
transition that touches more than one collection at once — claiming a duty writes the
duty and the agent row together — and a row rule can only scope one collection per
request. So the console reads directly (fast, and live over a channel) and posts every
change through the function, which runs at organization level and can do the whole
transition atomically.
`level` is READ for the same reason: it is a ceiling on which endpoints an identity
token may call at all, and this app deliberately gives the browser none that write.
`tokens` is absent on purpose. Agent credentials are default-denied to browsers; the
console lists and revokes them through the function instead.
`attachments` is absent for the same reason, one step removed: the row is harmless but
the object it names is private, and the only way to open one is a short-lived URL the
function mints for a caller it has just checked. A browser that could read the rows
would learn what files exist without being able to open them, which is nobody's win.
Each read is an OR of two branches: rows you own, or rows on a board you are a member of.
Membership reaches a rule through the `boards` claim on your account, which the function
writes when an owner adds you (functions/src/members.js). Projects carry their id as
`slug`; everything else as `project_id`.
The claim must exist on every account, and must never be an empty list — a rule naming a
missing claim is a hard deny for BOTH branches, and `in []` is refused. The function keeps
it as ["-", ...boards], and the console asks it to heal the claim before its first read.
